QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_16

question.text: The portion of fund return that accrues to investors only, based on the hurdle rate, is known as:

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook defines the Hurdle Rate or Preferred Return as the threshold return for investors. Preferred return accrues only to investors, and incentive fees are paid only on the return earned over and above this preferred return. The Trap: Catch-up is a later tier of the distribution waterfall, NAV is a valuation concept, and alpha is excess return over a benchmark — none of these is the workbook's name for the hurdle-rate-linked investor-only return. Note: The preferred-return / hurdle-rate definition is taken from the AIF (Category III) Distributors workbook (Series XIX-B).
